translations.text: Historians say that there are three countries called India. The first India lies next to the kingdom of the Ethiopians, the second lies next to the Medes, and the third next to the great ocean;
this third India has darkness on one side, and the terrible ocean on the other.
God's apostle Bartholomew came to this country. He went into the temple of the idol Astaroth and lived there as a stranger.
In that idol-temple lived a devil who spoke to people through the image and healed the sick, the blind and the lame, whom he himself had harmed before.
The idol harmed people's sight and afflicted their bodies with various illnesses. Then it answered them through the image, saying that they should offer it their sacrifices and it would heal them;
But he did not help them with any real healing. When they turned to him, he stopped the bodily affliction, because he then owned their souls.
then foolish people thought that he healed them, when he stopped afflicting them.
Then, when the apostle went into the temple, the devil Astaroth fell dumb and could not help any of those he had harmed, because the holy servant of God was near.
Many sick people lay there inside the temple, and every day they made offerings to the idol.
But when they saw that it could not help them, or answer anyone, they went to a nearby city where another devil was worshipped,
whose name was Berith. They made offerings to him and asked why their god could not answer them. The devil Berith then answered and said,
"Your god is bound so tightly with iron chains that he does not dare even to breathe or speak, ever since God's apostle Bartholomew came into that temple."
They asked, "Who is this Bartholomew?" The devil answered,
"He is a friend of Almighty God, and he has come to this region to bring to nothing all the idols that these Indians worship."
They said, "Describe his face to us, so that we can recognize him." Berith answered them,

"He has black, curly hair and a white body. He has prominent eyes, a moderate nose, and a full beard, a little grey. He is of medium height, and he is clothed in a white outer garment, and within the space of twenty-six years:
his clothing has not become dirty or worn out, and his shoes have not worn through. He bends his knees a hundred times by day and a hundred times by night, praying to his Lord.
His voice is like an enormous trumpet, and God's angels travel with him, and they do not let hunger or any weariness harm him.
He is always of the same mind and stays cheerful. He foresees and knows all things, and he knows the language of every people."
Even now he knows what I am saying about him, because God's angels serve him and make all things known to him.
When you look for him, you will find him if he himself wishes it. If he does not wish it, you will truly not find him.
I beg you to pray him earnestly not to come here, in case the angels of God who are with him command me as they commanded my companion Astaroth." And with these words the devil fell silent.
They went back and examined the face and clothing of every foreign man, but in two days they did not find him at all.
Meanwhile, a madman cried out through the devil's spirit and said, "O apostle of God, Bartholomew, your prayers torment me and set me on fire."
Then the apostle said, "Be silent, you unclean devil, and leave the man."
And at once the man who had been mad for many years was cleansed of the foul spirit and spoke sensibly.
Then King Polymius heard about the madman, how the apostle had rescued him from his madness, and he had him summoned and said,
"My daughter is pitifully mad. Now I ask you to bring her back to her right mind, just as you did for Seustius, who had been tormented for many years with terrible madness."
The apostle saw the girl bound with hard chains, because she bit and tore anyone she could reach, and no one dared to come near her. Then the apostle ordered her to be unbound.
The servants answered him, "Who dares to touch her?" Bartholomew answered, "I have bound the fiend that tormented her, and you are still afraid of her.
Go and unbind her, and give her food, and bring her to me early in the morning." They did as the apostle commanded, and the cursed spirit could no longer torment her.
Then the next morning King Polymius loaded camels with gold, silver, precious gems and silk garments, and looked for the apostle, but he did not find him at all.
The morning after that, the apostle came into the king's chamber while the door was shut, and asked him, "Why did you look for me with gold and silver, and with precious gems and garments?
Those who seek earthly wealth need such gifts as these; but I truly desire no earthly treasure and no fleshly pleasure.
But I want you to know that the Son of Almighty God, who made the heavens and the earth and all creatures, humbled himself so that he was born from a virgin's womb.

He had a beginning in his human nature, though he never had a beginning in his divine nature. Rather, he himself is the beginning, and he gave a beginning to all creatures, both visible and invisible.
The virgin who bore him had refused any union with a man and had vowed her virginity to Almighty God.
God's archangel Gabriel came to her and announced that the heavenly Prince would come into her womb. She believed his words, and so she became with child."

The apostle then preached the whole Christian faith to the king, and the redemption of the world through the Saviour's coming, and how he overpowered the devil of hell and took mankind away from him. And he said,
"The Lord Christ, who overcame the devil through his innocent death, sent us throughout all nations to drive out the devil's servants,
those who dwell in images, and to snatch the heathens who worship them out of their power.
But we do not accept gold or silver. We despise it, just as Christ despised it, because we desire to be rich in his kingdom, where disease has no place,
nor sickness, nor sorrow, nor death. There is eternal happiness and blessedness there, and joy without end, with everlasting riches.
That is why I went to your temple. The devil who answered you through the idol has been made captive by the angels of God who sent me.
And if you submit to baptism, I will make you see the devil and hear by what trick he appears to heal sickness.
Ever since the accursed devil deceived the first-created man, he has had power over unbelieving people, more over some and less over others:
more over those who sin more greatly, and less over those who sin less.
Now the devil uses his tricks to make wretched people fall sick, and he entices them to believe in idols:
Then he stops the affliction and holds their souls in his power, once they say to the devilish idol, 'You are my god.'
But this devil who was inside your temple is bound, and he can in no way answer those who pray to him.
If you want to test whether I am telling the truth, I will order him to go into the idol, and I will make him confess this same thing: that he is bound and cannot give any answer."
Then the king answered, "Tomorrow this people intends to offer their gifts to him. I will come there then, so that I may see these wonderful deeds."
Indeed, on the next day the king came to the temple with the people of the city, and then the devil cried out through the image with a terrible voice and said,
"Stop, you wretches, stop your offerings, so that you do not suffer worse torment than I do.
I am bound with fiery chains by the angels of Christ, whom the Jews hanged on the cross. They thought that death could hold him captive;
but he truly overcame death. He bound our chief with fiery bonds, and on the third day he rose victorious. He gave the sign of his cross to his apostles and sent them out through all nations.
One of them is here, and he holds me bound. I beg you to intercede for me with him, so that I may go to some other region."
Then the apostle Bartholomew said, "You unclean devil, confess who harmed these sick people." The unclean spirit answered,
"Our chief, bound as he is, sends us to mankind so that we may harm them with various illnesses;
first their bodies, because we have no power over their souls unless they offer their sacrifices to us.
But when they make offerings to us for the health of their bodies, then we stop afflicting the body, because after that we have their souls in our power.
Then it seems as though we heal them, when we stop the injuries.
And people worship us as gods, when in truth we are devils, followers of the chief whom Christ, the Son of the Virgin, bound.

From the day that his apostle Bartholomew came here, I have been grievously consumed by burning chains, and therefore I speak because he commanded me; otherwise I would not dare to speak in his presence, nor would even our chief."
Then the apostle said, "Why will you not heal these sick people, as you used to do?" The demon answered,
"When we harm people's bodies but cannot harm the soul, the bodies remain in their injury."
Bartholomew said, "And how do you come to harm the soul?" The devil answered,

"When they believe that we are gods and make offerings to us, Almighty God abandons them. Then we leave the body unharmed and take hold of the soul that has turned to us, and it is then in our power."
Then the apostle said to all the people, "Now you have heard what kind of god this is that you believed healed you;
but hear now the true God, your Creator, who dwells in heaven; and from now on do not believe in vain images:
and if you want me to intercede with God for you, and want these sick people to receive health, then overthrow this image and break it to pieces."
If you do this, then I will hallow this temple in Christ's name and wash you inside it with his baptism from all sins." Then the king ordered the image to be thrown down.
So the people then eagerly threw ropes around it and heaved at it with poles; but because of the devil they could not move the image.
Then the apostle ordered the ropes to be untied, and said to the accursed spirit that was lodged in her,
"If you wish that I should not send you into the abyss, depart from this image, and break it, and go to the wilderness, where no bird flies, nor ploughman ploughs, nor does the voice of man sound."
He went out at once, broke the image piece by piece, and shattered all the carved images inside the temple.
Then the people cried out with one voice, "There is one Almighty God, the one whom Bartholomew preaches."
The apostle then stretched out his hands toward heaven and prayed: "Almighty God, in whom Abraham believed, and Isaac, and Jacob;
you who sent your only-begotten Son to redeem us with his precious blood from slavery to the devil, and who have made us your children;

You are the unbegotten Father; he is the Son, eternally begotten of you; and the Holy Spirit eternally proceeds from you and from your Son. He gave us this power in his name, that we should heal the sick.
and to give light to the blind, cleanse lepers, drive out devils and raise the dead. And he said to us, 'Truly I say to you, whatever you ask of my Father in my name will be granted to you.'
Now I pray in his name that this sick multitude be healed, so that they may all know that you alone are God in heaven, and on earth, and in the sea,
you who restore health through the same Lord of ours, who lives and reigns with you and with the Holy Spirit for ever and ever."
When they answered, "Amen," then all the sick multitude was healed;
and then there came flying an angel of God, shining like the sun, and he flew around the four corners of the temple, and carved with his finger the sign of the cross on the squared stones, and said,

"The God who sent me said that, just as these sick people are healed of all diseases, so he has cleansed this temple of the foulness of the devil, whom the apostle commanded to depart to the wilderness.
And God has commanded me first to show the devil before your eyes. Do not be frightened at the sight of him, but mark the sign of the cross on your foreheads, and every evil will depart from you."
And the angel then showed the people the accursed spirit in this likeness. He appeared like a huge Ethiopian, with a sharp face and a broad beard.
His locks hung down to his ankles, his eyes were shooting fiery sparks, a sulphurous flame came out of his mouth, he was dreadfully covered in feathers, and his hands were bound behind his back.
Then God's angel said to the hideous devil, "Because you were obedient to the apostle's commands and broke this devilish image,
now, according to his promise, I will unbind you, so that you may go to the wilderness, where no human being lives; and you shall stay there until the great judgment."
And the angel then unbound him, and he went away with pitiful wailing and never appeared anywhere again. Then the angel flew up to heaven while they all looked on.
Then King Polymius, with his wife and his two sons and all his people, believed in the true God and was baptized, and he cast off his crown together with his purple robes,
and would not forsake God's apostle. After this, all the perverse apostates gathered together, and accused the king before his brother Astyages, who was king over another people, and said,
"Your brother has become the follower of a sorcerer, who claims our temple for himself and breaks our gods."
Then King Astyages became enraged and sent a thousand armed soldiers to bring the apostle to him in bonds.
When the apostle was led to him, the king said, "Why have you corrupted my brother with your sorcery?" Bartholomew answered,
"I did not corrupt him, but I turned him from heathen worship to the true God." The king said to him, "Why did you overthrow our gods?" He answered,
"I gave the devils the power to smash the vain images in which they dwelt, so that the human people might turn from their errors and believe in the eternal God."
Then the king said, "Just as you made my brother forsake his god and believe in your god, so I will also make you forsake your god and believe in mine."
Then the apostle answered, "I showed the god whom your brother worshipped bound, and I ordered him to break his own image.
If you can do this to my God, then you will bend me to the worship of your god:
But if you cannot do this to my God, I will shatter all your gods, and then you must believe in the true God whom I preach."
While they were saying this, someone told the king that his greatest god, Baldath, had fallen and burst into pieces.
Then the king tore his purple robe and ordered the apostle to be beaten with hard clubs and afterwards beheaded. And so, martyred in this way on this day, he departed to the eternal life.
After this the brother came with his people, and they carried the holy body away with glorious hymns of praise. They built a church of wonderful size and reverently laid his holy relics in it.
On the thirtieth day, King Astyages, who had ordered the apostle to be killed, was seized by a fiendish spirit and went horribly mad.
Likewise all the perverse heathens who had spitefully accused the apostle before the king went mad together with him. They and he ran to his tomb, and there they died raving.
Then great fear and terror spread over all the unbelievers, and they then believed, and were baptized at the hands of the priests whom the apostle had ordained earlier.

Then the apostle Bartholomew revealed concerning the believing king Polymius that he should receive the office of bishop; and the servants of God and the believing people unanimously chose him for that office.
It happened then, after the ordination, that he worked many miracles in God's name through his faith, and continued twenty years in the bishopric, and in a good way of life;
and with perfected merits he departed to the Lord, to whom be honour and glory for ever and ever.
We may take an example from the apostolic teaching, that no Christian man should seek his healing except from the Almighty Creator,
whom life and death, sickness and health obey, who said in his gospel that not one little bird falls to its death without God's ordering.
He is so mighty that he arranges and orders all things without toil; but he afflicts his chosen ones with sicknesses, as he himself said,
"Those whom I love, I rebuke and chastise." For various reasons Christian people are made sick: sometimes for their sins, sometimes for testing,
sometimes for God's wonders, sometimes for the preservation of a good way of life, so that they may be the more humble; but in all these things patience is necessary.
Sometimes also, through God's vengeance, a very terrible evil comes upon the wicked man, so that his punishment begins in this world, and his soul departs to the eternal torments for his cruelty;
just as with Herod, who killed the innocent children at Christ's birth, and many others besides him.

If the sinful man is afflicted for his unrighteousness, then if he praises his Lord with patience and asks for his mercy, he is then washed from his sins through the sickness, just as a dirty garment is through soap.
If he is righteous, he then has greater merit through his affliction, if he is patient.
He who is impatient, and with a bitter mind complains against God in his sickness, has a twofold humiliation, because he increases his sins with that complaining, and suffers nonetheless.

God is the true physician, who heals the sins of his people through various chastisements. The worldly physician is not cruel, even though he treats the wounded man with cautery or with a surgical knife.
The physician cuts or burns, and the sick man cries out; yet he does not take pity on the other's lamenting, because if the physician gives up his skill, then the wounded man perishes.
So also God heals the sins of his chosen ones with various afflictions; and though it is grievous to the sufferer, nevertheless the good Physician wishes to heal him to eternal health.
Truly, he who suffers no affliction in this life goes to suffering.
For his own sins a man is made sick, just as the Lord said to a certain bedridden man who was carried to him, "My son, your sins are forgiven you: arise now, and carry your bed home."
For testing some men are made sick, as was the blessed Job, when he was righteous and obedient to God.

Then the devil asked that he might test him, and he then destroyed all his possessions in one day, and afterwards struck him himself with the greatest affliction, so that worms swarmed over his whole body.
But the patient Job, in all these misfortunes, did not sin with his mouth, nor speak anything foolish against God, but said,
"God gave me the possessions, and took them back from me again; blessed be his name." God then also healed him, and repaid him his possessions twofold.
Some people are afflicted for the sake of God's signs. Christ said this of a certain blind man, when his disciples asked him for whose sins the man had been born blind.
Then the Saviour said that he was born blind not for his own sins, nor for his kinsmen's, but so that God's wonder might be made manifest through him.
And at once he mercifully healed him, and showed that he is the true Creator, who opened the unformed eye-sockets with his healing spittle.
For the preservation of true humility God's chosen ones are very often afflicted, as Paul the apostle said of himself,
"There is given to me a stab in my body, and the devil buffets me, so that the greatness of God's revelations may not exalt me;
therefore I asked my Lord three times to take the devil's goad away from me; but he answered me, 'Paul, my grace is sufficient for you.'
Truly, strength is made perfect in weakness. Now I gladly glory in my weaknesses, so that Christ's power may dwell in me."
The Christian who is afflicted in any way like this, and then seeks his health through unlawful practices, or through accursed incantations,
or through any witchcraft, is like the heathens who made offerings to idols for the health of their bodies, and so destroyed their souls.
Whoever is sick should pray to his Lord for his health and bear the afflictions patiently,

for however long the true Physician sees fit, and should not buy his body's health with his soul through any craft of the devil. He should also ask for the blessing of good people, and seek his health at holy relics.

No Christian is permitted to seek his health at any stone, or at any tree unless it is the holy sign of the cross, or at any place unless it is God's holy house. Whoever does otherwise is without doubt practising heathen worship.
Yet we have the example in holy books that whoever wishes may treat his body with true medicine, as the prophet Isaiah did when he made a poultice for King Hezekiah's wound and healed him.
The wise Augustine said that it is not dangerous for someone to take a medicinal herb; but he condemns it as unlawful sorcery if someone ties the herbs on himself, unless he lays them on the wound.
Nevertheless, we should not set our hope on medicinal herbs, but on the Almighty Creator, who gave the herbs their power.
No one shall sing over herbs with incantations, but bless them with God's words, and so eat them.
Yet let everyone know that no one comes to the eternal rest without hardships, since Christ himself would not ascend to his own kingdom without great hardship;
so also his apostles and the holy martyrs bought the heavenly kingdom with their own lives;
and afterwards holy confessors also became holy through strict living in God's service, and through great abstinence and chastity.
What should we, who live at the end of this world, do if we are afflicted for our sins, except praise our Lord and humbly pray,
that he may lead us through the temporary afflictions to the eternal joy? To him be glory and praise for ever and ever. Amen.
